newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary Europool new fund takes assets to HUF13bln.
newsitem.headline: Hungary Europool new fund takes assets to HUF13bln.

text.p: Hungarian fund management company Europool Befektetesi Alapkezelo Rt launched a new open-ended fund with 250 million forints ($1.3 million) of initial capital, the fund's General Director Gyula Fater told Reuters.
The new fund, "Hunnia Reszveny Nyiltvegu Alap", will invest at least 40 percent of its capital in domestic stocks, he said.
Europool said in a statement the fund's planned initial capital was well oversubscribed on the back of an upbeat tone on the Budapest Stock Exchange.

"Investors subscribed for 250 million forints instead of the envisaged initial capital of 100 million forints, which was partly due to the current favourable situation on the bourse," the statement said.
On Wednesday the BUX index finished at a sixth successive closing high of 7,296.64 points, up 55.55.
Subscriptions for Europool's new fund ran between June 30 and July 2, and after one trading day on Tuesday the fund's capital had risen to above 280 million forints, Fater said.
Fater added Europool now manages 13 billion forints of assets in its funds, with 12 billion of this in open-ended funds.
Europool has so far managed eight funds, of which two already expired and two more closed-end funds will expire at the end of 1997. The other four funds are open-ended.
